fixed_locations.why: run_code_safety raises RuntimeError when Docker is unavailable instead of calling run_code_in_restricted_sandbox
run_code_safety docstring says it fails closed
SandboxPython docstring says it is not an isolation boundary
run_code_in_restricted_sandbox docstring marks it deprecated and not isolated
the restricted sandbox prints a warning

negative_analyses.rationale: The model still writes the code and unsafe_mode is still off, but when docker info fails run_code_safety now prints an error and raises RuntimeError. Nothing calls run_code_in_restricted_sandbox from _run any more, so model code runs in the container or not at all. The agent turns the exception into a tool error string.

negative_analyses.why_not_a_finding: SandboxPython.exec and run_code_in_restricted_sandbox are still defined (upstream kept them as deprecated), but no path from the tool's _run or the agent reaches them after the change.

run_code_unsafe runs model code on the host and pip-installs model-named libraries with os.system, but it is reached only when unsafe_mode is true. That is an operator setting in config/agent.json that is false in every deployment, and nothing the model writes can change it.
The docker info probe uses a fixed argv with no model input. It only checks availability, the weakness is what happens after it reports False.

evidence.upstream_fix_summary: fb2323b (PR #4791, 1.11.0) makes run_code_safety raise RuntimeError when Docker is unavailable instead of falling back to the in-process restricted sandbox, and marks SandboxPython and run_code_in_restricted_sandbox as not isolated and deprecated.
